where: next/tests/hooks/test_caller.py (test_property_junk_from_excluded_characters_never_approves, the between-quotes position and its comments)
problem: The fix makes every between-quotes draw carry one character from the single quote, U+0000 to U+001F and U+007F. A new comment says this means 'no draw can be a correct plain call whatever the seed'. That is false. The single quote and the tab are refused only inside a span. A drawn or inserted quote can close the span, and a drawn or inserted tab is then a legal separator before a second quoted argument. Seeds 4050 and 19019 both draw vsdd survey --flag value 'x'<TAB>'', which is a correct plain call. The grammar accepts it, the parser reads the arguments survey, --flag, value, x and an empty string, and sh, bash 3.2, bash 5.3, dash and zsh all run vsdd with exactly those arguments. With the code unchanged and the seed tuple set to (4050, 19019), the test fails on that text. The six seeds in the file pass only because they draw no such text, and 2 of seeds 0 to 19999 do. The precondition assertion holds for these texts, so it does not stop them. This is the fault class of step3-hook-runner-fix-5-C1-1, now much rarer: about one seed in 10000 instead of most seeds.
proposed_resolution: Leave the tab (U+0009) out of both between-quotes alphabets, both inside and refused. test_every_control_character_is_refused_between_quotes already pins a tab inside a span at code 0x09. Neither alphabet then holds a space or a tab. Any quote in the draw closes the span right before a non-blank character, so the regex refuses it, and every other refused character is refused anywhere in the text. A scan of seeds 0 to 19999 with this change finds 0 approved draws. Make the precondition assertion match, for example: inner holds a character below U+0020 other than a tab, or U+007F, or a quote. Correct the comment that says no draw can be a correct plain call, so it gives the reason that is actually true.

where: next/tests/hooks/test_caller.py (REFUSED_CALLS, test_allow_list_regex_refuses_the_tables_on_its_own); the rule is the program alternative of _CALL_TEXT_RE in next/plugins/vsdd-factory/py/vsdd/hooks/caller.py
problem: The program word has its own character classes in _CALL_TEXT_RE, a first class [A-Za-z0-9_./] and a rest class [A-Za-z0-9_@%+:,./-]. They are not built from _SAFE, and no test pins the excluded characters there. In a scratch copy I added each of the 21 excluded characters and the single quote to the rest class, and separately to the first class, which is 44 mutations. Every one kept all 77 tests in test_caller.py, test_shell.py and test_runner.py passing. Adding '=' to the first class also kept them passing. The parser gate does not stop these, so the regex is the only gate on the first word. Under such a widening, is_vsdd_call approves ./$x/vsdd survey, $hid/vsdd survey, ./*/vsdd survey, ~hid/vsdd survey, \hid/vsdd survey (parsed program hid/vsdd), a'hid'/vsdd survey (parsed ahid/vsdd), {x/vsdd survey, ;/vsdd survey and =/vsdd survey. In each case a variable, a glob, a tilde or zsh's equals expansion picks the program at run time, or the call is approved and can never run. Today's code refuses all of them. The gap is only that nothing pins the rule. It predates this round, but reverting each rule, as this confirmation was asked to do, shows it. It sits in the first word, which this unit tightened.
proposed_resolution: Add a deterministic test. For every excluded character c and the single quote, assert that ./a<c>b/vsdd survey and <c>x/vsdd survey are refused by caller._CALL_TEXT_RE alone and through is_vsdd_call. Add =/vsdd survey and =x/vsdd survey to REFUSED_CALLS. Then check in a scratch copy that each of the 45 mutations above fails at least one test.

where: next/tests/hooks/test_caller.py (REFUSED_CALLS, whose header claims 'One case per excluded character'); the rules are _SAFE, the argument prefix and the separator of _CALL_TEXT_RE in next/plugins/vsdd-factory/py/vsdd/hooks/caller.py
problem: Several argument-position rules fail no test when reverted, each in a scratch copy against the 77 tests in test_caller.py, test_shell.py and test_runner.py. (1) Adding '$' to _SAFE keeps every test passing, and is_vsdd_call then approves vsdd survey $x and vsdd survey a$b. The '$' row, vsdd survey $(id), also holds parentheses, so '$' is never the only reason a row is refused. (2) Adding '(' to _SAFE keeps every test passing. The '(' row, vsdd survey (x), also holds ')'. The parser still refuses vsdd survey a(b, so here the regex-alone test, which exists so that no hole hides behind the parsed shape, falls short. (3) Dropping (?!=) from the quoted prefix keeps every test passing, and is_vsdd_call then approves vsdd survey ='hid'. Under zsh -f, with EQUALS on by default, I checked that vsdd ='a' gives vsdd the path of the command a, not =a. (4) Letting a carriage return into the argument separator keeps every test passing, and is_vsdd_call then approves vsdd survey<CR>hid. Letting a newline into the separator, or a carriage return into the leading blanks, also keeps every test passing. The parser refuses those two, so the regex-alone gap remains. The current code refuses every one of these texts. Like C2-2, this predates the round but shows when each rule is reverted.
proposed_resolution: Add rows in which each rule is the only reason for refusal. Add vsdd survey $x, vsdd survey a$b, vsdd survey a(b, vsdd survey ='a', vsdd survey<CR>x, vsdd survey<LF>x and <CR>vsdd survey to REFUSED_CALLS, so the regex-alone test covers them. Alternatively, add a loop asserting that vsdd survey a<c>b is refused by the regex alone for every excluded character c. Then re-check in a scratch copy that adding '$' or '(' to _SAFE, dropping the prefix's (?!=), and widening the separator or the leading blanks with CR or LF each fail a test.
